result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): B gives one consistent set of values: a shared 80rem page width, a 66ch measure and three breakpoints that are all actually used. Its docs-column math checks out (about 664px at 1024px and about 656px at 1280px), and its CSS mostly uses the tokens it names. A has a clever full/wide/content breakout grid and a strong table and code treatment, but it uses two page maximums (80rem and 90rem), hard-codes values like 90rem and 72rem, and lists a 40rem breakpoint it never uses. That weakens its 'one set of rules' claim, though B's 4/8/12 column scheme is a bit heavier than these pages need. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): B wins narrowly. Its full/wide/content grid with named lines handles code blocks and tables better: they break out to a wider column and scroll inside it. It also covers very large monitors and mid-size screens explicitly. A is simpler and more consistent in its tokens, with one 80rem page width and no stray literals. B uses two page maximums (80rem and 90rem), hardcodes 72rem and 4rem, and adds fluid type and sticky table columns that the pages don't need.
